advanced-filter-card-dates-hint: Filter card dates with @createdAt, @receivedAt, @startAt, @dueAt, @endAt or @listEnteredAt. Example: @endAt >= '2026-01-01' or @endAt = none. Quote a custom field name that starts with @.
advanced-filter-description: Advanced Filter allows to write a string containing following operators: == != <= >= && || ( ) A space is used as a separator between the Operators. You can filter for all Custom Fields by typing their names and values. For Example: Field1 == Value1. Note: If fields or values contains spaces, you need to encapsulate them into single quotes. For Example: 'Field 1' == 'Value 1'. For single control characters (' \/) to be skipped, you can use \. For example: Field1 == I\'m. Also you can combine multiple conditions. For Example: F1 == V1 || F1 == V2. Normally all operators are interpreted from left to right. You can change the order by placing brackets. For Example: F1 == V1 && ( F2 == V2 || F2 == V3 ). Also you can search text fields using regex: F1 == /Tes.*/i

import-board-instruction-asana: Paste an Asana tasks export JSON ({ "data": [...] } from the Asana export or GET /tasks). Tasks are grouped into sections (memberships); completed tasks go to Done.
import-board-instruction-businessmap: In Businessmap (formerly Kanbanize), open Advanced Search, choose Configure results to pick the columns, download the Excel file, then choose that .xlsx file. Columns are read by their English names (Title, Column, Lane, Owner, Deadline ...): if your account uses another language, rename the header row to English first. Column becomes lists and Lane swimlanes; owners, tags, color, dates, comments and parent links keep their places, and Priority, Size, Type and other columns become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-clickup: In ClickUp, export the tasks as CSV (Settings, Imports / Exports, Export Items, or a List or Table view's export with all columns), then paste the CSV. Statuses become lists, ClickUp lists become swimlanes, and tasks become cards with their subtasks, assignees, tags, dates, priority and time.
import-board-instruction-csv: Paste in your Comma Separated Values(CSV)/ Tab Separated Values (TSV) .
import-board-instruction-deck: Paste a NextCloud Deck board JSON (a board with "stacks", each stack carrying its "cards"). Stacks become lists and cards become cards.
import-board-instruction-excel: Choose an .xlsx workbook: a table with one card per row (columns such as Title, Description, Status/List, Members, Labels, dates and custom fields), or a workbook WeKan exported, also one with every board on a sheet of its own. The next step shows which column is which field. Every sheet with a header row becomes a board.
import-board-instruction-focalboard: Unzip the .boardarchive file and paste a board's board.jsonl, with or without its version line. The board view's group-by property becomes the lists, other select properties become labels, text and checkbox blocks become the description and a checklist, and comments are kept. Images and attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-issues: Paste a __sourceName__ issues JSON array (__endpoint__). Issues become cards grouped into Open / Closed lists.
import-board-instruction-kanboard: Paste a Kanboard export JSON: an object with "columns" (or tasks carrying column_name) and a "tasks" array (title, description, column_name, swimlane_name, date_due, owner, tags). Columns become lists and tasks become cards.
import-board-instruction-kanri: In Kanri, open Import & Export and choose Export individual board (or Export all data), then paste the .json file. Columns become lists and cards become cards, with their description, due date, tags and colors; a card's tasks become a checklist. From an all-data export the first board is imported.
import-board-instruction-leo: Paste a Leo outline (.leo file). Top-level nodes become lists, their children become cards with the node body as the description, and deeper nodes become checklists. Marked nodes import as done.
import-board-instruction-linear: In Linear, export the issues as CSV (Settings, Import / Export, Export data, or a view's export), then paste the CSV. Statuses become lists, teams become swimlanes, and issues become cards with their assignee, labels, dates, parent issue, priority, estimate, project and cycle.
import-board-instruction-markdown: Paste a markdown task list (the convention markdown-kanban tools such as Obsidian Kanban use): "## List name" headings, with "- [ ]"/"- [x]" items underneath. Headings become lists and items become cards; a plain bulleted list with no checkboxes also imports, as open cards.
import-board-instruction-meistertask: In MeisterTask, click the project name, choose Export project and export the CSV, then paste it. Sections become lists and tasks become cards, with their notes, due date, assignee and tags; completed tasks keep their completion date. A CSV written for MeisterTask's own import works too.
import-board-instruction-monday: In monday.com, open the board menu, choose More actions and Export board to Excel (with updates and subitems if you like), then choose that .xlsx file. The Status column becomes lists and groups become swimlanes; people, dates, timeline and tags keep their places, other columns become custom fields and updates become comments.
import-board-instruction-notion: In Notion, open the database as a full page, choose ••• and Export, pick Markdown & CSV, and choose the .zip file it downloads, or one database CSV from it, or paste that CSV. A column named Status becomes the lists (without one, the first column that looks like a select does, and the import report says which); rows become cards with their title, tags as labels, people as members, dates, and the page text as the description; other columns become custom fields. Relations, images and attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-nullboard: In Nullboard, open the board, choose Export this board... from the menu, open the .nbx file in a text editor and paste its contents. Lists become lists and notes become cards: a note's first line is the card title and the rest its description. A raw note gets the label raw. A file with several boards imports its first board.
import-board-instruction-obsidian: In Obsidian, open the Kanban board's file as Markdown (or open the .md file in a text editor), then paste all of it. Lanes become lists with their card limits, cards keep their tags, dates, priority, fields and checklist, and the Archive becomes archived cards.
import-board-instruction-openproject: Paste an OpenProject work-packages collection JSON (GET /api/v3/work_packages). Statuses become lists and work packages become cards.
import-board-instruction-opml: Paste an OPML outline, as Workflowy, Dynalist, OmniOutliner, Logseq and other outliners export it. Top-level items become lists, their children become cards with the note as the description, and deeper items become checklists. Completed items import as done.
import-board-instruction-orgmode: Paste an Org mode file, as Emacs, Orgzly or Beorg write it. Top-level headings become lists and second-level headings become cards. TODO and DONE, priorities, tags, SCHEDULED, DEADLINE and CLOSED are kept, and checkboxes and deeper headings become checklists.
import-board-instruction-pivotal: In Pivotal Tracker, open the project's MORE tab and choose Export CSV (or select stories and choose Bulk Actions, CSV), then paste the CSV. Each story state becomes a list and stories become cards, with their type and labels, owners, requester, dates, comments, tasks and blockers; Estimate becomes Story points and iterations become sprints.
import-board-instruction-plane: In Plane, open Workspace Settings, choose Exports, export the projects as JSON, CSV or Excel and download the .zip file, then choose that file, or one file from inside it, or paste the JSON or CSV. States become lists, projects become swimlanes, and issues become cards with their identifier, parent, assignees, labels, dates, links and comments; priority, estimate, cycle and module become custom fields. Plane's export has no descriptions or attachments, so they are not imported.
import-board-instruction-planner: In Microsoft Planner, open the plan, choose the ⋯ menu next to its name, then Export as Excel (in classic Planner: Export plan to Excel), and choose that .xlsx file. Buckets become lists and tasks become cards, with their assignees, dates, labels, checklist and description; Progress, Priority and Completed By become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-quire: In Quire, open the project menu and choose Export CSV, then paste the CSV. Statuses become lists and tasks become cards, with their subtasks as child cards, assignees, tags as labels, start, due and completed dates, description and priority as a custom field. Comments and attachments are not in Quire's CSV.
import-board-instruction-redmine: In Redmine, open the project's Issues, choose Also available in: CSV at the bottom of the list, pick the columns (All columns, with Description) and export, then paste the CSV. Redmine names the columns in your language, so set your language to English in My account before exporting. Each status becomes a list and issues become cards, with the tracker as a label, assignee, author, dates, parent task and related issues; priority, category, target version, estimated time, % Done and custom fields become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-superproductivi: In Super Productivity, open Settings, then Sync & Backup, choose Export Data and paste the contents of the sp-backup .json file. Each project becomes a swimlane and tasks become cards in To Do, In Progress, Backlog or Done, with their notes, tags, due date, time spent and sub-tasks; archived tasks become archived cards.
import-board-instruction-taiga: In Taiga, open Admin > Project > Export and download the project dump (unpack a .json.gz file first), then paste its JSON. User story statuses become lists, user stories become cards with their tasks as subtasks, epics and issues get swimlanes of their own, and sprints, tags, comments and custom attributes come along. Attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-tasksorg: In Tasks.org, open Settings, Backups and choose Export tasks, then paste the contents of that .json file. Lists become lists and tasks become cards, with their notes, tags, dates, comments and subtasks; completed tasks keep their completion date, and priority becomes a custom field.
import-board-instruction-taskwarrior: Paste the output of task export: a JSON array, or one task per line. Completed tasks go to Done, project and priority become labels, annotations become comments, and depends becomes blocked-by dependencies.
import-board-instruction-teamwork: In Teamwork.com, fill in the Excel task import template (Tasklist, Task, Description, Assign to, Start date, Due date, Priority, Estimated time, Tags, Status) and save it as .xlsx, then choose that file. Task lists become lists and tasks become cards; a task starting with -, # or > becomes a subtask of the task above it (--, ## or >> one level deeper). Assignees, dates and tags keep their places; Priority, Estimated time and Complete become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-ticktick: In TickTick, open Settings, Account, Backup & Import and generate a backup, then paste the CSV file. Each TickTick list becomes a swimlane and its columns become lists; tasks keep their tags, dates, checklist, priority and subtasks.
import-board-instruction-todoist: In Todoist, open the project, choose the ⋯ menu at its top right, then Manage data > Export as CSV, and paste the CSV file. Sections become lists, tasks become cards, sub-tasks become a checklist, notes become comments, and @labels and priorities p1 to p3 become labels.
import-board-instruction-todotxt: Paste a todo.txt file: one task per line, as the todo.txt app and compatible apps write it. Completed tasks ("x") go to Done, +project and @context become labels, (A) becomes a priority label, and due: and t: become due and start dates.
import-board-instruction-vikunja: In Vikunja, open Settings, choose Data Export and download the .zip file it sends you, then choose that file, or paste the data.json inside it. Kanban buckets become lists and tasks become cards, with their labels, assignees, dates, description, task lists as checklists and comments; priority, percent done and done become custom fields. Attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-wrike: In Wrike, export a project or folder to Excel, or fill in Wrike's Excel import template, then choose that .xlsx file. Folder and project rows become swimlanes, Status becomes lists and tasks become cards, with their Key, parent task, assignees, start and end dates, dependencies and description; Priority, Duration and other columns become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-zenkit: Paste a ZenKit list export JSON ({ "title", "stages":[...], "items":[...] }). Stages become lists and items become cards.
import-file-label: Choose the export file, or paste its text below:
import-here-instruction: Import a WeKan export (.json or .zip) here:
import-members-map: Your imported board has some members. Please map the members you want to import to your users
import-members-map-note: Note: Unmapped members will be assigned to the current user.
import-members-mode-map: Choose an existing user for each of them
import-members-mode-placeholder: Keep them as placeholder users with their own names, to map to real users later
import-not-wekan-export: That file is not a WeKan export
import-one-board-per-project-hint: Each swimlane the import would make (a project, folder or list of the tool) becomes its own board. Parent cards and dependencies between those boards are listed in the import report.
import-report-description: The board was created, but some parts of the file could not be brought over. The same report is kept in Admin Panel → Problems → Recovery.
import-too-large: The file is too large to import at once. Split it into smaller files, for example by project or by date, and import each one.
instance-desc: Every signed-in user of this WeKan can view this board. It is never shown to people who are not signed in. Only people added to the board can edit.
invalid-file: If filename is invalid, upload or rename is cancelled.
invalid-year: Invalid year. Please type all four digits, for example 2026.
just-invited: You are just invited to this board
list-permissions-desc: What each role may do in this list, over what the board allows. Board admins can always edit.
list-select-cards: Select all cards in this list
muted-info: You will never be notified of any changes in this board
name: Name
notification-delivery-invalid: The setting could not be saved.
notification-delivery-layout-clear: Clearly arranged: board, who, card in bold
password-change-required-text: This site now requires passwords of at least __min__ characters, and yours is shorter. Choose a longer one to continue. Every session of your account is then signed out, and you sign in again with the new password.
password-length-from-environment: A value set in the server's environment is in effect; saving here overrides it.
password-length-report-desc: Accounts that signed in with a password shorter than the minimum length. Only the browser knows how long a password is, so it reports a short one after signing in; the password and its length never leave it. Fixed is when the account's password was changed - an account that signs in with a short password again is shown as too short again.
password-min-length-description: Signing in with a shorter password is listed below. Signing in is never refused for it.
password-min-length-enforce-description: A shorter new password is refused, and an account that signs in with a shorter password must change it before anything else. Changing it signs every session of the account out. LDAP, OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, CAS and Sandstorm passwords are their provider's, and are not checked.
password-pwned: This password has appeared in a data breach. Choose another one.
password-same-as-username: The password must not be the username or the email address.
password-too-short: The password must be at least __min__ characters long.
preview-pdf-not-supported: Your device does not support previewing PDF. Try downloading instead.
private-desc: This board is private. Only people added to the board can view and edit it.
public-desc: This board is public. It's visible to anyone with the link and will show up in search engines like Google. Only people added to the board can edit.
r-add-actinguser-member: Add the user who triggered this rule as a member
r-blocks-conflict: This rule changed while you were editing. Reload the saved rule before saving.
r-blocks-help: Connect one trigger to one action. Drag blocks from the toolbox. Use the form editor for advanced options.
r-blocks-invalid: Connect exactly one trigger to one action. Remove disconnected or extra blocks before saving.
r-blocks-permission: Board administrator permission is required to edit rules.
r-blocks-unavailable: Rule data is unavailable. Use the form editor to review this rule.
r-cron-invalid: A cron schedule has five fields: minute hour day month weekday.
r-d-move-to-bottom-gen: Move card to bottom of its list
r-d-move-to-top-gen: Move card to top of its list
r-email-members-hint: A board member added from the list goes into To as @username and is sent to that member's own email address. Other email addresses can still be typed into To.
r-import-paste: Paste exported rules (JSON or CSV) or Trello Butler commands here
r-import-trello: Import rules from Trello Butler (best effort)
r-import-trello-note: Trello board exports do not contain Butler rules. Paste Butler command text here to map the supported subset; unmapped lines are reported.
r-import-workflow-note: Import a visual workflow exported from n8n or Node-RED. Recognized trigger/action nodes are mapped to WeKan rules; unmapped nodes are reported.
r-import-wrike-workflow-done: Wrike workflow "__name__": __lists__ list(s) and __rules__ rule(s) added, __skipped__ part(s) not read
r-insert-variable: Insert variable into the last text field:
r-moved-back: moved back to an earlier list
r-moved-forward: moved forward to a later list
r-remove-all: Remove all members from the card
r-remove-all-assignees: Remove all assignees from the card
r-rule-title-required: Please enter a title for the rule
r-rules-not-shown: Only board admins see this board's Rules.
r-trigger-vars-hint: List, swimlane, title, checklist and user fields also accept {creator}, {assignees}, {members} and {customField:Name}, read from the card when the rule is checked.
r-vars-people-hint: Also: {creator}, {assignees}, {members} (usernames in text, email addresses in To) and {customField:Field name}. These also work in member, list and swimlane names of other actions.
r-when-a-card-is-moved: When a card is moved to another list
r-when-a-card-title-or-description-conta: When a card's title or description contains
r-when-a-due-date-changed: When the due date is set or changed
r-when-a-end-date-changed: When the end date is set or changed
r-when-a-received-date-changed: When the received date is set or changed
r-when-a-start-date-changed: When the start date is set or changed
r-when-card-date: When this date of a card
r-when-card-in-list: When a card has been in list
r-workflow-help: Drag a trigger and an action into the builder, then add the rule. Drag an action onto an existing rule to change what it does.
r-wrike-workflow-note: A Wrike workflow is a list of statuses, each in the Active, Completed, Deferred or Cancelled group. Export writes this board's lists as one, named after the board, in the JSON Wrike's API returns for workflows: create that workflow in Wrike before importing the board's Wrike Excel export, so its statuses are applied. Import reads that JSON pasted above, from WeKan or from Wrike's GET /workflows, into the chosen board: a status without a list becomes a list, and a rule marks a card complete when it is moved into a Completed or Cancelled status and incomplete in an Active or Deferred one. Wrike's own automation rules cannot be exported from Wrike.
recovery-no-events: No recovery events recorded. The database is healthy.
recovery-report-desc: Automatic data-safety and remediation actions: corruption detection, text-data backups, restores, re-migration from MongoDB, and automatic repair of a bloated database.
restore-all-skipped-wip-limit: __count__ card(s) were not restored: their lists have reached their WIP limits. Restore them one at a time to choose another list.
restore-card-no-list-with-room: Every list on this board has reached its WIP limit. Raise a limit, or move or archive cards, to restore this card.
restore-card-wip-limit-reached: The list __list__ has reached its WIP limit. Restore the card to another list:
scrum-backlog-help: Order work by backlog rank. Assign cards to a planned or active sprint.
scrum-confirm-cancel: Cancel this sprint? Its cards retain their membership until reassigned.
scrum-confirm-close: Close this sprint and save its results? Unfinished cards will move to the selected destination.
scrum-daily-empty: No daily observations have been recorded for this sprint.
scrum-daily-observations-export-help: First recorded observation of each UTC day; missing days are omitted. Observations do not record every change or end-of-day totals. Unknown estimates are not zero.
scrum-daily-observations-help: Each bar shows the first recorded observation of a UTC day, at the timestamp shown. Missing days are omitted. These observations do not record every change or show end-of-day totals. Unknown estimates are not zero. Use this section's Export action for daily observations; the toolbar Export action exports sprint results.
scrum-daily-truncated: Only the most recent 366 observations are shown.
scrum-edit-sprint: Create or edit a planned sprint
scrum-history-checkpoint-ask-admin: A board administrator can roll it back or keep the board as it is.
scrum-history-checkpoint-counts: __applied__ of __total__ changes were written, __pending__ were not, and __conflicted__ were changed by someone else since.
scrum-history-checkpoint-discard: Keep the board as it is
scrum-history-checkpoint-discard-confirm: Keep every record as it is now, including the changes the stopped operation already wrote?
scrum-history-checkpoint-hint: Rolling back puts every changed record back as it was before; it is offered only when nobody else has changed those records since. Keeping the board as it is removes the stopped operation and changes no records. Either way, it is recorded in Admin Panel, Problems, Recovery.
scrum-history-checkpoint-stuck: An undo, redo or restore of Scrum changes stopped on a conflict. Scrum edits on this board are blocked until it is resolved.
scrum-import-card-ambiguous: A card matches more than one card on this board: __reference__
scrum-import-card-not-matched: A card was not found on this board: __reference__
scrum-import-card-on-another-board: A card belongs to another board and was left unchanged: __reference__
scrum-import-into-board: Import Scrum planning into this board
scrum-import-into-board-done: The Scrum planning was imported and recorded in History.
scrum-import-into-board-hint: Choose a WeKan board export or Scrum transfer file. Sprints and releases this board already has are linked, never duplicated. Cards are matched by ID, or by card number and title; cards that do not match are listed and left unchanged. Preview first to see what will change.
scrum-import-invalid-file: This file is not valid JSON.
scrum-import-pending: The Scrum import is incomplete. Scrum edits and report exports are unavailable.
scrum-import-preview-cards: Cards: __updated__ to update, __unchanged__ unchanged, __unmatched__ not matched
scrum-import-preview-nothing: Nothing to change: this board already has this planning.
scrum-import-preview-releases: Releases: __created__ new, __matched__ already on this board, __skipped__ not imported
scrum-import-preview-sprints: Sprints: __created__ new, __matched__ already on this board, __skipped__ not imported
scrum-import-record-ambiguous: A sprint or release matches more than one on this board: __reference__
scrum-import-record-not-imported: A sprint, release or event could not be imported: __reference__
scrum-import-reference-omitted: A source reference could not be restored: __reference__
scrum-import-sprint-finished: A card was not moved into a finished sprint: __reference__
scrum-no-closed-sprints: No closed sprint snapshot is available.
scrum-partial-report: Partial report: only cards currently assigned to you are included.
scrum-partial-snapshot: This sprint contains only part of the original snapshot.
scrum-releases-select-help: A card can be in several releases. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) to choose more than one; clear them all to remove the card from every release.
scrum-report-help: Reports retain estimates from sprint snapshots. Unknown estimates are counted separately; they are not zero estimates. Compare velocity only across matching estimate units and policies.
scrum-scope-history: Scope and burndown, change by change
scrum-scope-history-empty: No changes since the sprint started.
scrum-scope-history-help: Replayed from the board's History since the sprint started: one row for each change to the sprint's cards, estimates or completed work.
scrum-scope-history-inconsistent: History does not reproduce this sprint's own snapshot: some changes were made without History, so these values are incomplete.
scrum-scope-history-truncated: Only the first changes could be read; the replay is incomplete.
scrum-select-sprint: Select a sprint to view its report.
submit-on-enter-description: When on, pressing Enter saves the card title, description and other inline editors; Shift+Enter inserts a new line. When off, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter saves and Enter inserts a new line.
text-contains-trigger-description: Matches when a card is created, or its title or description is changed, and the new text contains this (case-insensitive).
title: Title
tracking-info: You will be notified of any changes to those cards you are involved as creator or member.
watching-info: You will be notified of any change in this board
webhook-hide-identity: Leave my name out of outgoing webhooks
webhook-payload-description: What outgoing webhooks (Rocket.Chat, Slack, ...) send. Default keeps the inherited setting; with nothing set, webhooks send what they always have.
webhook-payload-field-details: Details: comment, description, values and dates
webhook-payload-field-links: Links to the card and board
webhook-payload-field-people: The member or assignee it is about
